newsitem.title: UK: British hospital staff mishandle inhalers - study.
newsitem.headline: British hospital staff mishandle inhalers - study.

text.p: Nearly a quarter of people suffering from asthma cannot use their inhalers correctly -- but British hospital staff often cannot do much better, a report published on Wednesday found.
Tests in a major British hospital showed none of the nurses in the accident and emergency department, and only two of the doctors, were able to correctly demonstrate how to use an inhaler.

Dr John O'Donnell of the Edinburgh Royal Infirmary said his survey of 25 senior house officers and 25 nurses showed medical staff needed better training in the use of inhalers -- which can save the lives of asthmatics.

"(The study) documents major deficiencies in the knowledge and skills in the accident and emergency staff with regard to correct use of MDIs (inhalers)," O'Donnell wrote in the Journal of Accident and Emergency medicine. REUTER MMF
